title: Separating V(I) from the closure of the image of V(J) by one element
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal of $R$ and $J\subseteq S$ an ideal of $S$. If the closure in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the image of $V(J)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}S$ under $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is disjoint from $V(I)$, then there is an element $f\in R$ whose image in $R/I$ is $1$ and with $\varphi(f)\in J$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07M3 (lemma-separate-image-closed-from-closed) and its proof (uses Algebra, Lemma Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology)

proof.text: *The closure of the image.* Put $I'=\varphi^{-1}(J)$, an ideal of $R$. The closure in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the image of $V(J)$ under $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is $V(I')$ [lem-weil-pbc-closure-image-spec-zero-locus]. (Stacks takes any ideal $I'$ with $V(I')$ equal to that closure, which exists since closed subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are of the form $V(I')$; we take this particular one.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M3 (lemma-separate-image-closed-from-closed), first sentence ('Let I' be an ideal such that V(I') is the closure of the image of V(J)'), with the choice I' = phi^{-1}(J) made by the agent (Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00FL)

proof.text: *$I+I'=R$.* By hypothesis $V(I)\cap V(I')=\emptyset$ (step 1). Hence $I+I'=R$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-zero-loci-disjoint-unit-ideal], and there are $g\in I$ and $f\in I'$ with $1=g+f$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M3, second and third sentences ('hence I + I' = R by Algebra, Lemma lemma-Zariski-topology. Write 1 = g + f with g in I and f in I'') (Algebra Lemma Tag 00E0, parts (8), (10))

proof.text: *Conclusion.* $f=1-g$ with $g\in I$, so the image of $f$ in $R/I$ is $1$. And $f\in I'=\varphi^{-1}(J)$ means $\varphi(f)\in J$. (Stacks, with an arbitrary $I'$, only gets $V(\varphi(f))\supseteq V(J)$, hence $\varphi(f)^n\in J$ for some $n$ by Algebra 00E0 (7), and replaces $f$ by $f^n$, still $\equiv1$ mod $I$; with $I'=\varphi^{-1}(J)$ one has $n=1$ and this step is not needed.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M3, last three sentences ('We have V(f') ⊃ V(J) ... Replacing f by f^n we win'), simplified to n = 1 by the choice of I' in step 1
